revisions.title: Finding your stock
revisions.summary: Use Stock by material for an overall view, then open a material or the Lot Register to see individual batches.
revisions.body_markdown:
Stock by material brings together ingredient and packaging quantities. Use the search and filters to find a material, identify shortages, or see which materials are below their buffer.

Open a material to see its current position, open lots, supplier listings, and movement history. The Lot Register shows each batch separately, including its internal lot code, supplier batch, status, and remaining quantity.

Check the displayed unit before comparing quantities. Ingredient stock is measured by mass; packaging stock is measured in units.

revisions.title: Understanding stock quantities
revisions.summary: Physical stock is what the records say you hold. Available stock excludes quarantined quantities and stock already reserved for production.
revisions.body_markdown:
- **Physical:** the balance of recorded stock movements.
- **Quarantined:** physical stock held out of availability.
- **Reserved:** stock allocated to production from released lots.
- **Available:** released physical stock minus its active reservations.
- **Incoming:** quantities still expected from ordered or partially received purchase orders. They are not yet physical stock.
- **Required:** production demand still needing stock, after existing reservations.

**Forecast = Available + Incoming − Required.** Existing reservations are already reflected in Available and are not deducted again through Required.

For example, 10 kg of released stock with 3 kg reserved leaves 7 kg available. With 4 kg incoming and another 5 kg required, the forecast is 6 kg.

A negative forecast signals a planning shortage. Check the relevant production demand and incoming orders; a forecast does not mean the goods have arrived.

revisions.title: Working with lots and status
revisions.summary: A lot represents one batch of material. Released and Quarantined describe whether it is available; Exhausted describes its remaining balance.
revisions.body_markdown:
The internal lot code identifies the batch in Soapkraft. Keep the supplier batch number as well when available, so you can trace the material back to its source.

**Released** stock can contribute to availability. **Quarantined** stock is kept out of availability while you review it. Changing handling status does not add or remove physical stock.

A lot is shown as **Exhausted** only when both its physical quantity and active reserved quantity are zero. A negative balance, or a zero balance with an active reservation, still needs attention and remains open.

Use the Lot Register filters to include exhausted lots or find a specific batch. A material's Open lots section shows up to ten lots; use View all lots for the complete register.

revisions.title: Entering stock you already hold
revisions.summary: Use Add stock manually in the Lot Register to enter an existing batch that has not yet been recorded in Soapkraft.
revisions.body_markdown:
Choose the correct material and supplier listing, enter the quantity already on hand, and check the unit and cost. The listing determines the entry unit and currency. Record the supplier batch, expiry date, and stock date where applicable.

The app creates an internal lot code and an opening stock movement. Use a date of today or earlier.

Enter each batch separately when you need separate traceability. Do not enter a batch manually if it is already recorded through a goods receipt: that would count the same stock twice.

If an existing lot has the wrong remaining quantity, use Adjust stock on that lot instead of creating another opening entry.

revisions.title: Recording an incoming delivery
revisions.summary: A purchase order contributes to Incoming stock. Posting a goods receipt records the quantities actually received as physical stock.
revisions.body_markdown:
Use the receiving workflow in Purchasing for a supplier delivery. Check the material, received quantity, unit, supplier batch, and any expiry information before posting the receipt.

A draft receipt does not increase physical stock. Posting creates the stock records for the received quantities. For a partial delivery, record only what arrived; the outstanding order quantity remains incoming.

Avoid also entering the same delivery through Add stock manually. Use the receipt as the source for tracing purchased stock.

If a received lot is quarantined, its physical quantity is recorded but it does not contribute to Available stock until released.

revisions.title: Correcting a lot quantity
revisions.summary: Use Adjust stock when a recorded lot balance differs from what you actually hold. The correction is added to its movement history.
revisions.body_markdown:
Open Adjust stock on the affected lot and choose the operation:

- **Set counted quantity:** enter the total quantity now present in that lot.
- **Add quantity:** enter only the amount to add to its current balance.
- **Remove quantity:** enter only the amount to subtract.

Check the unit, select the reason, and add a note when needed. An Other reason requires a note. Review the resulting balance before saving.

The adjustment preserves the original receipt and adds a correction movement. It does not cancel production reservations. If the new balance leaves reserved stock uncovered, review the warning and the affected production work.

If stock changes while the adjustment is open, reload and review the current balance before trying again.

revisions.title: Understanding reserved stock
revisions.summary: A reservation allocates a lot quantity to production. It reduces availability without changing the physical stock balance.
revisions.body_markdown:
For a released lot, Available is its Physical quantity minus active reservations. The same material can have reservations across several lots.

Manage allocations from the relevant production work. Reserving material is not the same as consuming it: consumption is recorded through production stock movements.

The Required figure in the material overview and forecast covers demand still needing stock after reservations, so allocated quantities are not counted twice.

If a stock adjustment reduces a lot below its reserved quantity, the reservations are not automatically removed. Review the affected allocations before continuing production.

revisions.title: Setting a stock buffer
revisions.summary: A buffer is the minimum available quantity you want to keep for a material. It helps you spot when stock is running low.
revisions.body_markdown:
Open the material details to set or change its buffer. Use the displayed unit and choose a quantity appropriate for your working stock.

The app marks the material as below buffer when its Available quantity falls below that level. Use the Below buffer filter in Stock by material to find these materials together.

A buffer does not reserve a lot, create a purchase order, or change physical stock. It is a planning threshold. Review production needs and incoming orders before deciding what to buy.

Clearing the buffer removes the threshold without changing stock or reservations.

revisions.title: Locating stored stock
revisions.summary: A storage location records where a lot is kept. A material can also have a usual storage location for new stock entries.
revisions.body_markdown:
Use the lot's location control when a batch moves to another storage area. Changing its location does not change its quantity or handling status.

On the material details page, set a usual storage location when most new batches go to the same place. Check the location on each entry; changing the usual location does not relocate existing lots.

Storage locations are enabled separately from production locations in workspace settings. When storage locations are disabled, their controls are hidden and existing assignments are retained.

revisions.title: Reading a material’s movement history
revisions.summary: The activity section explains how physical stock changed over the selected period, from its opening balance to its closing balance.
revisions.body_markdown:
Choose the period you want to review. Opening physical stock is the balance before that period; Closing physical stock includes its recorded movements.

Receipts and other inbound movements add stock. Production consumption and other outbound movements subtract it. Adjustments record corrections. The reconciliation line brings these amounts together so you can compare them with the closing balance.

Use a movement's source link to inspect the related record. Adjustment details show the reason, recorded user, and before-and-after quantities where available.

Changing the period or page only changes what you see. It does not alter stock. Reservations affect availability, but reserving a quantity alone does not create a physical stock movement.
